name: BD+76 227B

boundTo.source: El-Badry, Rix & Heintz (2021, MNRAS 506, 2269) list TOI-1710 and BD+76 227B in their Gaia EDR3 wide-binary catalogue (VizieR J/MNRAS/506/2269, source_id 1116613161053977472 and 1116612783096856960), 3,609 AU apart on the sky, with a chance-alignment probability of 3.8e-5: the pair is bound. No orbit of the pair is published, and the Gaia astrometry alone does not constrain one, so the star is placed by its own astrometry and carries no orbit.

description: Star bound to TOI-1710, 3,609 AU away.

radius.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the radius of TIC 445805957 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

mass.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the mass of TIC 445805957 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

temperature.source: Stassun et al. (2019), AJ 158, 138 (TIC v8.2), the effective temperature of TIC 445805957 (VizieR IV/39/tic82)

text.card: BD+76 227B is a star of 3,470 K, bound to TOI-1710 3,609 AU away.
text.introduction: BD+76 227B shares its motion through space with TOI-1710, 3,609 AU away, so the two are a bound pair. Both are placed where Gaia measures them.

notes: BD+76 227B's orbit around TOI-1710 is not measured; both stars are placed at their Gaia DR3 positions, which is where they are
